newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary plans to buy out Alitalia stake in Malev.
newsitem.headline: Hungary plans to buy out Alitalia stake in Malev.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt said on Wednesday that it proposed to the government that APV buy out Alitalia's 30 pct stake in national air carrier Malev Rt.
"We would like to replace Alitalia with another strategic investor," APV managing director Benedek Belecz told a news conference.
He added that APV planned to start negotiations with Alitalia as soon as the government approves the plan, hopefully by the end of June.
Belecz also said APV would like to complete the buyout by the end of the year.
"APV plans to find new strategic and financial investors for Malev and would like to list the company on the Budapest Stock Exchange in 1998 or 1999," Belecz said.
Alitalia bought a 30 percent stake in Malev in 1992, while five percent was purchased by the Italian state company Simest.
The company has registered capital of HUF 7.69 billion, and Alitalia holds pre-emption rights to acquire further shares by the end of 1998.
APV Rt owns 63 percent of shares, and under the privatisation law a decisive minority stake of 25 percent plus one vote must remain in permanent state ownership.
At the same time, the scheme seeks to preserve the national character of the airline company by leaving 50 percent plus one vote with Hungarian shareholders.
